ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, $\triangle ABE\cong \triangle ADC\cong \triangle ABC$, if $\angle 1=150^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle \alpha$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle ADC \cong \triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle E = \angle DCA$, and $\angle BAE = \angle 1 = 150^\circ$,\\
since $\angle EFD = \angle CFA$, and $\angle \alpha + \angle E + \angle EFD = \angle EAC + \angle DCA + \angle CFA$\\
it implies that $\angle EAC = \angle \alpha$;\\
Given that $\angle EAC = 360^\circ - \angle BAE - \angle 1 = 360^\circ - 150^\circ - 150^\circ = 60^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle \alpha = \boxed{60^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the figure, B and C are below, A is at a lower internal position, E is above; from the figure it can be seen that D is located on the slanted line BE, F is the intersection point of AE and DC; angle 1 is marked at point A at ∠BAC, α is marked at point D and is an angle belonging to triangle EFD. Reasoning: according to the given same-order congruence △ABE≅△ABC, the corresponding angles ∠BAE=∠BAC can be obtained, and in the figure ∠BAC=∠1=150°, so ∠BAE=150°. Also from △ABE≅△ADC, get ∠AEB=∠DCA. Because D is on BE, and F is on AE and DC, so in △EFD and △ACF, ∠EFD and ∠CFA are vertical angles and are equal; and ∠E=∠DCA. Thus the third angles of the two triangles are equal, namely α=∠EAC. Around point A, ∠BAE, ∠BAC, and ∠EAC combine into a full angle, therefore ∠EAC=360°−150°−150°=60°. So α=60°.
